In mathematics, particularly, in [[mathematical analysis|analysis]], '''Carleman's condition'''  gives a sufficient condition for the determinacy of the [[moment problem]]. That is, if a [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] <math>\mu</math> satisfies Carleman's condition, there is no other measure <math>\nu</math> having the same [[moment (mathematics)|moments]] as <math>\mu.</math> The condition was discovered by [[Torsten Carleman]] in 1922.<ref>{{harvtxt|Akhiezer|1965}}</ref>

==Hamburger moment problem==

For the [[Hamburger moment problem]] (the moment problem on the whole real line), the theorem states the following:

{{math theorem|name=Carleman's condition|
Let <math>\mu</math> be a [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]] on <math>\R</math> such that all the moments
<math display=block>m_n = \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} x^n \, d\mu(x)~, \quad n = 0,1,2,\dots</math>
are finite. If
<math display=block>\sum_{n=1}^\infty m_{2n}^{-\frac{1}{2n}} = + \infty,</math>
then the moment problem for <math>(m_n)</math> is ''determinate''; that is, <math>\mu</math> is the only measure on <math>\R</math> with <math>(m_n)</math> as its sequence of moments.
}}

==Stieltjes moment problem==

For the [[Stieltjes moment problem]], the sufficient condition for determinacy is
<math display=block>\sum_{n=1}^\infty m_{n}^{-\frac{1}{2n}} = + \infty.</math>

==Generalized Carleman's condition==
In<ref> M. Nasiraee, Jav. Kazemitabar and Jal. Kazemitabar, "The Bijection Property in the Law of Total Probability and Its Application in Communication Theory," in IEEE Communications Letters, doi: 10.1109/LCOMM.2024.3447352.</ref> Nasiraee et al. showed that, despite previous assumptions,<ref>S. S. Shamai, “Capacity of a pulse amplitude modulated direct detection photon channel,” IEE Proceedings I (Communications, Speech and Vision), vol. 137, no. 6, pp. 424–430, Dec. 1990.</ref> when the integrand is an arbitrary function, Carleman's condition is not sufficient, as demonstrated by a counter-example. In fact, the example violates the [[bijection]], i.e. determinacy, property in the probability sum theorem. When the integrand is an arbitrary function, they further establish a sufficient condition for the determinacy of the moment problem, referred to as the ''generalized Carleman's condition''.
